issue_context.title: EVP_PKEY_derive() no longer accepts buffers larger than expected output
comments:
This does seem to be a bug. For clarity this looks like HKDF only and the check in question looks a little different now to what it looked like when it was first introduced. The check is now here:

https://github.com/openssl/openssl/blob/5f4b3db624a83b812f23412e698ffd9c4284f87a/providers/implementations/kdfs/hkdf.c#L441-L448

Simply changing `!=` to `<=` would seem sufficient, although we should also have a test for this.

> Simply changing != to <= would seem sufficient, although we should also have a test for this.

Unfortunately, I do not believe this is sufficient.  The new signature for HKDF_derive() has prk_len as an in-variable only, and it is not (and cannot be) updated here to the actual output length.

@mattcaswell was unfortunately looking in the wrong place.  The KDF implementation "HKDF" is called with `EVP_KDF_derive()`, not `EVP_PKEY_derive()`, and the implementation is behaving correctly according to documentation:

> **EVP_KDF_derive()** processes any parameters in *Params* and then derives
> *keylen* bytes of key material and places it in the *key* buffer.  If the
> algorithm produces a fixed amount of output then an error will occur
> unless the *keylen* parameter is equal to that output size, as returned
> by *EVP_KDF_CTX_get_kdf_size()*

`EVP_PKEY_derive()` calls a KEX implementation, so the spot to look would be this:

https://github.com/openssl/openssl/blob/926c698c6f0a197e0322d4617db0ecd0d40f6e06/providers/implementations/exchange/kdf_exch.c#L91-L105

Notably, you do find a `EVP_KDF_derive()` call here...  but it seems that the code doesn't do enough to adapt the data to fit the requirements when calling `EPV_KDF_derive()`, so it ends up calling it with an `outlen` that's too large.
@jeredfloyd, would you mind testing the modification from #18533?
@levitte Thanks!  I'll try this patch against the RHEL 9 package and report back; if it works I will also submit it internally as a proposed backport.
@jeredfloyd, hold on...  that patch isn't quite right
I've added a test in a separate PR, #18536

> @jeredfloyd, hold on... that patch isn't quite right

I think I got it right, now

review_comments: This looks odd. Why is this necessary?

Because depending on the mode (EXTRACT_AND_EXPAND, EXTRACT_ONLY or EXPAND_ONLY), the output size may be fixed or indefinite.  Kinda documented here:

https://github.com/openssl/openssl/blob/d2399d8cd29f56e6614f0b3db4e7e563a745902a/doc/man3/EVP_KDF.pod?plain=1#L157-L160
